subject: Pilot eval plan: recommended models, dataset spec, and runbook
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novadyne.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot eval plan: recommended models, dataset spec, and runbook

Hi Elena — great conversation earlier. Short recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth and can kick off the pilot quickly.

Quick recap of needs (as I heard them):
- Use-case: clinical triage assistant that summarizes intake notes and suggests next-step codes/triage levels.
- Priority metrics: accuracy of triage label, precision on safety-critical classes, and hallucination rate on factual fields.
- Throughput: target 150 qps peak for POC (we'll tune later).
- Data: 4k de-identified triage examples for an initial run; CSV export is fine.

Proposed Redwood evaluation plan (high level):
1) Dataset intake: You upload a sanitized CSV following the attached novadyne_eval_template.csv (columns: id, prompt, ground_truth_label, reference_response, meta_json). See section "Dataset format" below for column notes.
2) Model candidates: we recommend running the pilot against these variants:
   - open-13b-ql (quantized fast path) — baseline for throughput/cost;
   - instruction-tuned-13b (higher instruction-following for label extraction);
   - open-33b-safety (stronger factuality/safety priors).
   I'll attach model_profiles_snapshot.pdf with perf/cost estimates per 1k tokens.
3) Scoring: Redwood will run automated scorers (exact match for label, semantic similarity for free-text fields) + a small human review sample (100 cases). We'll provide an evaluation report with token cost, latency P50/P90, and confusion matrices.
4) Timeline: dataset and NDA paperwork in 1 week -> dry-run in 2 weeks -> full 4k execution in week 3.

Immediate asks from Novadyne:
- Upload the sanitized CSV to the Drive link I shared. Include a short mapping doc that defines label taxonomy (if any).
- Confirm whether you want the human review to be Novadyne reviewers or Redwood's small panel.

Attachments: novadyne_eval_template.csv, prompt_bank_v1.md, model_profiles_snapshot.pdf (attached to this thread).

If that looks right, I can schedule the intake + kickoff meeting next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

--
Note: cost estimates in the attached PDF are for evaluation runs only and exclude reserved capacity discounts.

From: Elena Morales <elena@novadyne.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot eval plan: recommended models, dataset spec, and runbook

Thanks Rishi — this captures the call well. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we upload: 

1) Dataset: we'll provide 4,200 de-id rows. The intake will come from our analytics SRE (procurement@novadyne.com will loop them in if needed). Are meta_json fields allowed to contain nested arrays for multi-symptom flags?
2) Labels: our taxonomy has 6 triage levels (0-5). Can Redwood support multi-label scoring if a case maps to two labels?
3) Human review: we'd prefer Novadyne clinicians to do the 100-sample review; will Redwood provide a scorer template/UX for that?

Also — small ask on governance: our security team wants a statement on data retention for POC artifacts (where will logs/kv-cache traces be stored and for how long?).

If the answers are straightforward I'd like to get the CSV up by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director, Clinical Operations | Novadyne Health
elena@novadyne.com
+1 (617) 555-4412

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novadyne.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot eval plan: recommended models, dataset spec, and runbook

Hi Elena — answers inline and a few concrete artifacts attached.

1) meta_json fields: yes, the intake supports JSON strings. For multi-symptom arrays use a JSON-encoded string in the meta_json column. We'll parse and preserve arrays as metadata only; scoring runs rely on the prompt + ground_truth_label columns.

2) Multi-label scoring: supported. Redwood's scorer will compute per-class precision/recall and a set-based F1 for multi-label cases. Please flag rows that are intentionally multi-label in a boolean column (is_multilabel) so we can apply the correct scorer.

3) Human review UX: we will provide a simple web scoring UI that Novadyne clinicians can use (row-by-row view with compare to model outputs). We'll export reviewer decisions into the same schema for reconciliation. I'll include a short sample export format in the prompt_bank_v1.md attachment.

Security/data retention: for Hosted POC runs (our default):
- Input artifacts: retained for 30 days in an encrypted S3 bucket (AES-256), access logged.
- KV cache & runtime traces: redacted traces retained for 14 days; full traces only kept if customer opts in for debugging.
- Derived evaluation reports (aggregated metrics): retained for 12 months.
We can support a 0-day retention or VPC/private deployment for customers who require no persistence beyond the request lifecycle; happy to include language in the SOW.

Model recommendations rationale (short):
- open-13b-ql: run-first baseline to measure latency/cost. Good for strict throughput targets.
- instr-13b: expected to reduce label extraction errors vs. the baseline on free-text prompts.
- open-33b-safety: run on the same dataset to check factuality regressions and safety-critical false positives.

Run specifics I need from you to start the dry-run:
- Upload the CSV to the shared Drive (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/ND-4721/benchmarks). Use file name novadyne_eval_v1.csv.
- Confirm whether reviewers are "novadyne_clinician" or "redwood_review_panel" (exact string needed for our reviewer gating).
- Provide your preferred dry-run window (we have slots: May 11-13, morning PST).

Attachments in this message: novadyne_eval_template.csv (format example), prompt_bank_v1.md (sample prompts + reviewer export), model_profiles_snapshot.pdf (perf & cost).

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for May 11 morning if you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novadyne.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot eval plan: recommended models, dataset spec, and runbook

Looping in next steps from an operations standpoint. Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. When you drop novadyne_eval_v1.csv into the drive:
- We'll validate format within 24 hours and send back a small schema report (missing cols, sample size, multilabel tags).
- If you confirm Novadyne clinicians for the human review, we'll provision the scoring UI and invite 3 reviewers; please send their emails to procurement@novadyne.com so we can create reviewer accounts.
- Dry-run slot tentatively booked: Tue May 11 09:00 PST (30 min). I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm the CSV upload.

Operational notes:
- We will run the three model candidates in parallel during the dry-run to gather latency/cost tradeoffs; total tokens billed will be included in the report.
- If you need a shortened retention window for the POC we can switch to an ephemeral-run mode (no artifact retention) but need the request ahead of the dry-run.

Marissa
Principal Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
